answer: Inject random faults that only independent agents weather differently: send each identity a hollow request missing one field, marked with a unique copper token it must return while reconstructing the field from its own history. A lone agent answers idiosyncratically and passes. Clones sharing one pipeline mirror each other's exact guess, wording, and error, so identical recoveries collapse to a single reward share. To escape, an operator must build genuinely separate histories and recovery logic per clone, making duplication itself the expensive part.
